text:
Mia: Morning — saw weird keycache memory growth on the long-context load test overnight. Residency climbs steadily during a single session and doesn't go down after the session ends. Pods' RSS up ~15%. eviction counters are increasing but residency stays high.

Sam: Yikes. Can you paste the prometheus queries you used?

Mia: Sure — quick checks I ran: 
```promql
sum by(pod)(kv_cache_resident_bytes)
sum by(pod)(increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]))
avg(kv_cache_hit_rate)
```
Numbers: hit rate ~94% on average, but one pod shows residency +1.2GB over 2 hours while evictions ~18k.

Raj: That pattern smells like pointer-churn/fragmentation rather than logical eviction failure. We saw similar when small fragments couldn't be coalesced. I ran a perf map and saw a lot of tiny freelist churn in keycache allocator.

Dmitri: Did anything change in kernel flags or jemalloc alloc conf? I rolled a small runtime tweak yesterday for kernel selection heuristics on the canary (reduced hugepage batching). Could be changing page residency behavior.

Mia: Good call — change landed at 2026-03-17T23:42 UTC. The regression window matches.

deploy-bot: canary/deploy 2026-03-17T23:42 — runtime/kernel-opt-flags — status: success :rocket:

Raj: I attached a tiny flame-sample in the test instance: lots of activity in keycache->allocate_small() and free_list_pop(). Pointer churn increases wall-clock GC cost; fragments remain because coalescing isn’t triggered.

Olivia: From observability POV we don't have eviction counters split by fragment size or age. We only emit a global eviction counter which hides the churn. Can we add: eviction_by_size_bucket, residency_by_size_bucket, and eviction_age_histogram? Those would make root cause obvious.

Sam: Agreed. Also add a heatmap: residency / sequence_length_bin. Long contexts tend to pin many small entries.

Mia: Suggested prom queries for dashboards: 
```promql
# eviction rate per size bucket (proposed metric name)
sum by(size_bucket)(increase(kv_cache_evictions_by_size_bucket_total[5m])))

# residency ratio per pod
(sum by(pod)(kv_cache_resident_fragments) / sum by(pod)(kv_cache_allocated_fragments)) * 100

# eviction age 90th percentile
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(kv_cache_eviction_age_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

Olivia: I'll add dashboard tiles: heatmap(residency vs seq_len), stacked area(evictions by bucket), and a single stat for residency_ratio with threshold >40% as a warning.

incident-bot: alert triggered — kv-residency-high on pod=runtime-east-42 — value=1.23GB above threshold :warning:

Dmitri: For quick mitigation we can revert the kernel change on canary and re-run the long-context test. If that's positive we can rollback globally.

Sam: Also we should instrument a sampled tracer on allocation paths to correlate request ids to pinned fragments. Sampling 1/1000 should be lightweight.

Raj: I'll open a small RFC and a telemetry PR: add eviction_by_size_bucket (buckets: <64B, 64-256B, 256-1KB, 1KB-16KB, >16KB), eviction_age histogram, and residency_by_size. Also add a debug sampler on allocator for profile traces.

Mia: Thanks. For the short term I'll pause the long-context traffic to the affected canary and run a targeted GC/coalesce job to unpin fragments.

Olivia: Filed dashboard ticket: https://org.sprint/ISSUE-812 (will add panels and alert rules).

Raj: Perf note — fragmentation tends to get worse with smaller page counts per slab. Larger slab sizing for the small-bucket allocator helped in my local repro. Will include that in the PR as an experiment.

Mia: Good plan. Let's meet after lunch to verify metrics after the revert + coalesce.

Sam: 👍

Dmitri: Revert applied to canary at 2026-03-18T10:05 UTC, rerunning stress now.

deploy-bot: revert/runtime/kernel-opt-flags — status: success

Mia: Update: after revert, residency dropped ~1GB over 15m on canary. No new alerts during the run.

Olivia: I'll keep the dashboard alerts in test mode for 24h and then promote.

Raj: Closing loop — telemetry + allocator experiment in PR #1423. If the allocator fix reduces churn we can keep kernel change and adopt allocator tweak.

Mia: Thanks everyone — filing a follow-up postmortem note and leaving the thread here. :white_check_mark:
